reference: TOML syntax and the documented shell binding/query API define literal contract expectations. The emission operation has an independent Python tomllib decoder on both arms and compares decoded values, not formatting; this is semantic adapter parity, not a GNU toml CLI.
coverage: TOML validation and scalar, boolean, indexed-array queries
TOML types, table keys, and empty-array count
parse variable bindings for nested tables, scalar arrays, and arrays of tables
escaped basic strings and UTC datetime decoding
Independent tomllib decoding of emitted nested tables, arrays of tables, strings, booleans, floats and datetime values.
exclusions: No GNU TOML CLI exists; query and binding cases use explicit contracts.
No full TOML conformance corpus or TOML 1.1-specific independent parser is provided. The independent tomllib emission fixture uses the common TOML 1.0 subset.

cases.purpose: Confirm Bash exposes toml as a builtin and that its registered help documents the parser and query interface.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t toml) == builtin ]]
help_text=$(help toml)
[[ $help_text == *'TOML v1.1.0 parser'* ]]
[[ $help_text == *'toml parse FILE'* ]]
[[ $help_text == *'toml get FILE KEY'* ]]
printf 'metadata-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Check a valid document, a nested integer selected by array index, a boolean's documented 0/1 value, and array cardinality.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' 'title = "example"' '[app]' 'ports = [80, 443]' 'enabled = true' > app.toml
toml validate app.toml
[[ $(toml get app.toml title) == example ]]
[[ $(toml get app.toml 'app.ports[1]') == 443 ]]
[[ $(toml get app.toml app.enabled) == 1 ]]
[[ $(toml type app.toml app.enabled) == bool ]]
[[ $(toml count app.toml app.ports) == 2 ]]
printf 'query-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Exercise TOML scalar/container type names, top-level and nested table-key enumeration without depending on key order, and the zero count for an empty array.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' 'number = 7' 'ratio = 1.5' 'flag = false' 'event = 1979-05-27T07:32:00Z' 'labels = []' '[service]' 'port = 9' > types.toml
[[ $(toml type types.toml number) == int ]]
[[ $(toml type types.toml ratio) == float ]]
[[ $(toml type types.toml flag) == bool ]]
[[ $(toml type types.toml event) == datetime ]]
[[ $(toml type types.toml labels) == array ]]
[[ $(toml type types.toml service) == table ]]
[[ $(toml count types.toml labels) == 0 ]]
mapfile -t top_keys <<< "$(toml keys types.toml)"
[[ ${#top_keys[@]} -eq 6 ]]
contains_key() {
  local want got
  want=$1
  for got in "${top_keys[@]}"; do
    [[ $got == "$want" ]] && return 0
  done
  return 1
}
contains_key number
contains_key ratio
contains_key flag
contains_key event
contains_key labels
contains_key service
mapfile -t nested_keys <<< "$(toml keys types.toml service)"
[[ ${#nested_keys[@]} -eq 1 && ${nested_keys[0]} == port ]]
printf 'types-keys-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Check the documented uppercase variable mapping for nested scalars, booleans, scalar arrays, and arrays of tables.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' 'title = "fixture"' 'enabled = true' 'names = ["red", "blue"]' '[server]' 'port = 8080' '[[workers]]' 'name = "one"' '[[workers]]' 'name = "two"' > parsed.toml
toml parse -V CFG parsed.toml
[[ $CFG_TITLE == fixture ]]
[[ $CFG_ENABLED == 1 ]]
[[ $CFG_SERVER_PORT == 8080 ]]
[[ $CFG_NAMES_LEN == 2 && $CFG_NAMES_0 == red && $CFG_NAMES_1 == blue ]]
[[ $CFG_WORKERS_LEN == 2 ]]
[[ $CFG_WORKERS__0_NAME == one && $CFG_WORKERS__1_NAME == two ]]
printf 'parse-bindings-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Check the documented -A interface binds full dotted TOML paths and scalar-array length/index entries into a Bash associative array.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' 'title = "fixture"' 'names = ["red", "blue"]' '[server]' 'port = 8080' > assoc.toml
declare -A DOC=()
toml parse -A DOC assoc.toml
[[ ${DOC[title]} == fixture ]]
[[ ${DOC["server.port"]} == 8080 ]]
[[ ${DOC["names.len"]} == 2 ]]
[[ ${DOC["names[0]"]} == red && ${DOC["names[1]"]} == blue ]]
printf 'assoc-bindings-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Check that a TOML basic-string newline escape is decoded as a newline in the queried string value.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' 'message = "first\nsecond"' > values.toml
toml get values.toml message

cases.purpose: Check the documented ISO 8601 rendering of a UTC TOML datetime and get -V binding without stdout output.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' 'at = 1979-05-27T07:32:00Z' > values.toml
value=$(toml get values.toml at)
[[ $value == 1979-05-27T07:32:00Z ]]
toml get values.toml at -V WHEN
[[ $WHEN == 1979-05-27T07:32:00Z ]]
printf 'datetime-binding-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Ensure validate rejects a syntactically incomplete TOML array with failure status and a diagnostic, as required by TOML syntax and the documented validate contract.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' 'items = [1,' > invalid.toml
if toml validate invalid.toml 2> diagnostic.txt; then
  exit 1
else
  rc=$?
fi
[[ $rc -eq 1 && -s diagnostic.txt ]]
printf 'invalid-rejected\n'

cases.purpose: Check canonical emission for a one-key integer document against an independently hand-encoded TOML representation.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' 'answer=42' > source.toml
toml emit source.toml > emitted.toml
[[ -s emitted.toml && $(<emitted.toml) == 'answer = 42' ]]
printf 'emit-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Emit mixed TOML and independently decode every emitted value with Python tomllib on both arms. Formatting/tree comparison is disabled only because semantically equivalent TOML formatting varies; both original and emitted files remain available as evidence.
cases.script:
cat > source.toml <<'TOML'
title = "first\nsecond"
enabled = true
ratio = 1.5
at = 1979-05-27T07:32:00Z
names = ["red", "blue"]
[server]
port = 8080
[[workers]]
name = "one"
[[workers]]
name = "two"
TOML
if [[ $(type -t toml) == builtin ]]; then
  toml emit source.toml > emitted.toml
else
  cp source.toml emitted.toml
fi
/usr/bin/python3 - <<'PY'
import tomllib
from pathlib import Path
source = tomllib.loads(Path('source.toml').read_text())
emitted = tomllib.loads(Path('emitted.toml').read_text())
def same(a, b):
    assert type(a) is type(b), (type(a), type(b), a, b)
    if isinstance(a, dict):
        assert a.keys() == b.keys(), (a.keys(), b.keys())
        for key in a:
            same(a[key], b[key])
    elif isinstance(a, list):
        assert len(a) == len(b)
        for left, right in zip(a, b):
            same(left, right)
    else:
        assert a == b, (a, b)
same(source, emitted)
print('independent TOML semantics preserved')
PY
